text:
olivia: quick sync — we got the new oak-30B checkpoint from research. want to triage quantization priority and hand off a calibration sweep. goal: find a config that hits <=2.5x hosted cost target while keeping instruction-following delta <1.5% on our eval set.

samir: sounds good. what's the baseline (float32) perf and our latency budget?

olivia: baseline tokens/sec ~ 95 @ 2048 context (p99 token-latency 70ms). latency SLO for hosted tier is 120ms p99, so headroom for quantized variants.

rachel: for evals let's use: 1) instr-follow eval (our instruction suite), 2) naturalness BLEU-ish checks, 3) safety regressions. sample size 1k prompts seeded from prod slices.

diego: I'll run the first smoke sweep. can you drop the conversion steps and target precisions? i can start with INT8 symmetric, FP8 e5b, and GGUF float16 fallback.

olivia: plan i'd propose: 
- step A (smoke, <4h): gguf export -> run FP16 baseline inference (verify results).
- step B (calib sweep, 24h): per-layer int8 static + post-training scale calibration (use 10k tokens sample) + fp8 asymmetric sweep.
- step C (quality triage, 8h): run instruction eval + safety suite on top 3 configs.
- step D (cost/latency bar): run batching profile and estimate token cost delta.
- step E (handoff): package winning config + conversion script + eval report for eng-platform.

samir: for step B can we use two calibration modes: minmax and KL-divergence? previous models responded well to KL. also add kv-cache priming for 512 prefix.

rachel: add acceptance gates: 
- instr-follow drop <=1.5% absolute, 
- safety regression: no new high-severity flags, 
- perplexity shift <2% on the dev set.

diego: copying commands i'll run: 
```bash
# export gguf
python tools/convert.py --checkpoint path/to/oak-30b.ckpt --out oak-30b.gguf --dtype float16

# calib sweep (int8 static vs fp8)
python tools/calibrate.py --model oak-30b.gguf --modes int8_fp8 --calib-samples 10000 --save-dir /tmp/calib_oak30b
```

olivia: perfect. add CI job + tagging so eng-platform can pick it up. use label `quant:onboard:oak-30b` and ping them when step C passes.

samir: what about streaming/serving compatibility? some int8 kernels break continuous KV. add a streaming smoke with 1-token streaming for 200 tokens.

rachel: noted. include a small prompt-set that stresses long-term memory (multi-turn).

diego: kicked off smoke export now. i'll post interim logs here. ETA for step A: ~90m.

calib-bot: job 5639 started: gguf export for oak-30B. logs -> https://ci.internal/jobs/5639 :rocket:

olivia: thanks diego. next: after smoke, if FP16 baseline matches research numbers, proceed to full calib sweep. i'll draft the evaluation template and share a PR to evals repo with the slices.

samir: if we get >1% drop on instr-follow for int8 static, we can test mixed-int8/FP16 hybrid (key/value in fp16). that often recovers quality.

rachel: and document the cost math (per-token GPU seconds -> $/k tokens) so product understands tradeoffs.

diego: quick status update: export finished, baseline FP16 matches within 0.8% of research perf. starting calibration runs (int8/kl, int8/minmax, fp8-e5b). posting logs as they land.

calib-bot: job 5642 completed: fp16 baseline inference smoke (match 0.8%). job 5643 queued: calib-run-int8-kl.

olivia: great. once diego has top-3 configs, i'll schedule a 30-min handoff with eng-platform tomorrow morning (block on calendar). tagging @eng-platform leads in the handoff invite.

samir: one more ask — collect example prompts where quantized models degrade. put them in the issue so we can use them for regression alerts.

rachel: agreed. add a summary table in the PR: config | instr-delta | safety-regressions | p99-latency | est-cost-multiplier.

diego: will do. posting the first calib logs now: https://ci.internal/logs/5643.

olivia: thanks team. moving to action. :white_check_mark:
